content:
maria.support: @customer-jane thanks for the report — can you drop the request_id you saw in the response headers?

customer-jane: sure — saw this on 2026-03-16 around 14:22 UTC. response header x-request-id: req_20260316_azx9e7 (sorry truncated in ticket)

maria.support: that helps. can you confirm the exact API path and a minimal curl you used? also include whether you used our hosted API or a dedicated endpoint.

customer-jane: GET /v1/generate with body { prompt: "..." } on hosted. curl: 

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..."
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":50}'
  --compressed
```

maria.support: thx. josh.ops can you try a quick log lookup for req_20260316_azx9e7? customer seeing 502 / timeout and high latency.

josh.ops: on it. quick note: centralized kibana only keeps request index for 7d, hotstore 30d but older ones may be in cold S3. if this is Mar 16 and today = Mar 17 we should be fine. searching...

josh.ops: kibana query I used (copy/paste):

```
request_id:"req_20260316_azx9e7" OR headers.x-request-id:"req_20260316_azx9e7"
index: rwd-requests-*
sort: @timestamp desc
```

josh.ops: got a handful of entries from the edge LB and the inference gateway — timestamps line up. main error: "upstream prematurely closed connection" from runtime pool at 14:22:07 UTC. attaching trace id trace_0a1b2c3d.

ingrid.eng: can you paste the runtime logs for that trace? if it's an OOM or kernel fault we want the pod logs + dmesg from that host. josh, are there core dumps?

josh.ops: pod logs attached in the debug bundle I uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/2026-03-16/req_20260316_azx9e7-bundle.tar.gz). bundle includes: gateway logs, runtime logs, k8s events. no core files present. there is a repeated line in runtime: "kvcache miss cause recompile slowdown" — not sure if related.

maria.support: customer, can you run a repro curl that includes the header we can correlate with logs? include X-Debug-Label so it shows up in request metadata: 

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..."
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Debug-Label: jane-req-20260316"
  -H "X-Request-Id: jane-local-1234"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","prompt":"same prompt","max_tokens":50}'
```

customer-jane: running now, I get a 502 again. response headers: x-request-id: req_20260316_azx9e7, x-runtime-trace: trace_0a1b2c3d

maria.support: perfect — that's exactly what we needed. i've escalated to eng and linked the S3 bundle. ingrid, josh, quick triage checklist: 1) check runtime pod metrics around 14:20-14:25 UTC (mem/cpu/oom_kills) 2) check network egress errors and nginx timeouts 3) grep the runtime for "upstream prematurely closed" + stack traces 4) confirm if this request used a cached KV shard or forced cold load

ingrid.eng: on it. initial look: pod shows elevated memory ~92% then brief spike to 99% around 14:22 and kube evicted a background worker. not a full OOM kill but enough to stall kernel. correlates with "kvcache miss" spikes.

josh.ops: noted. retention note for support: index.rwd-requests-* hot indices rotate every 24h, kept 7d, then moved to cold. if customers ask for >7d you need to request archive retrieval (takes ~2-4h). debug bundle contains the S3 pointer for cold logs as well.

maria.support: customer, we'll keep you posted. next steps: eng will try to repro with the same payload and labels, we may ask you for a debug window to run a few more calls. for billing/latency concerns we'll open a follow-up ticket if we find retry storms or throttling issues.

customer-jane: appreciate it — available for a 30m window tomorrow 14:00 UTC if you want to repro live. :thumbsup:

ingrid.eng: thanks everyone. i'll attempt a local repro in a staging path that mirrors runtime caching (same model, same shard config). if I can reproduce I'll propose a mitigation (increase cache warm threshold or bump pool size) and a post-mortem.

debug-bot: debug bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-debug/2026-03-16/req_20260316_azx9e7-bundle.tar.gz (size: 28MB)

maria.support: closing the loop here after eng triage: initial root cause likely cache coldstart + transient memory pressure causing upstream disconnects. ops put an autoscale bump on the pool for the next 6h while we roll a fix. will update with final RCA in postmortem.

customer-jane: thanks for the fast help!
